Accounting measurement is a basic feature of financial accounting, and it occupies an important position in the theory and methods of financial accounting. Which of the following statements about accounting measurement attributes is incorrect? ____
options:
A.Historical cost reflects the past value of an asset.
B.Replacement cost is the current cost of acquiring an identical or similar asset.
C.Present value is the cash or other equivalent that needs to be paid currently to acquire an asset.
D.Fair value refers to the price that would be received to sell an asset or paid to transfer a liability in an orderly transaction between market participants on the measurement date.
answer:
financial.completion:
C.Present value is the cash or other equivalent that needs to be paid currently to acquire an asset.
explanation:
1. Present value refers to the amount obtained by discounting future net cash flows at an appropriate discount rate; it is a measurement attribute that takes into account factors such as the time value of money.

screening_snapshot.question_plan: Ask which laboratory upgrade is guaranteed to have the lowest present-value cost among packages eligible for installation before a merger's First Effective Time. Require identification of the source's nitrile–nitride mixing hazards and, as an explicit project assumption, controls addressing both hazards. Use the retrieved merger consent language, and stipulate that every package triggers two hypothetical negative covenants; G, A, and B have written Parent consent covering both, while U has consent covering only one. G addresses flammable gas only; U, A, and B address both hazards. Installation costs for G, U, A, and B are respectively 50, 60, 100, and 108 thousand dollars. Over five years, their continuous annual maintenance cost rates c(t), in thousands, lie respectively between 1 and 2, 1 and 2, 2 and 3, and 2 and 4, each bound multiplied by (1.10)^t. Assume integrable cost rates, a 10% effective annual discount rate, no other costs or residual values, and continuous payment. Request eligibility decisions, present-value cost bounds, and a guaranteed recommendation without assuming exact maintenance paths.

answer_plans.plan: Identify flammable gas generation and heat generation, excluding G because it lacks heat controls. Apply written Parent consent across all negative covenants before the First Effective Time, excluding U because one triggered covenant remains unconsented. Discount continuous maintenance payments using c(t)/(1.10)^t and bound the five-year integral by five times its lower and upper rate bounds. Adding installation costs gives G [55,60], U [65,70], A [110,115], and B [118,128] thousand dollars. Recommend A: it is eligible and its maximum cost is below B's minimum cost.

Recognize flammable gas generation but omit heat generation, mistakenly accepting G as chemically suitable. Correctly exclude U on consent grounds and calculate all discounted cost bounds, but recommend G because its interval is below those of A and B.

Correctly identify both chemical hazards, explain the all-covenant written-consent requirement, and calculate all four present-value intervals. Nevertheless, rank every package together and recommend G without applying the chemical and contractual eligibility findings to the financial comparison.

Identify both hazards and correctly understand that G has written consent covering every triggered covenant, but incorrectly treat contractual consent as overriding the project's requirement to address both chemical hazards. Admit G despite its missing heat controls and recommend it using otherwise correct discounted cost bounds.

Makes the merger covenant relevant to the proposed installation timing.

financial.necessity: Treats the maintenance payment stream as part of the upgrade's present-value cost.
Uses the assumed 10% rate to convert future payments into present amounts.
Requires discounting rather than directly totaling the increasing nominal maintenance rates.

mathematics.necessity: Multiplies the discounted rate's lower bound by five years to bound maintenance cost from below.
Multiplies the discounted rate's upper bound by five years to bound maintenance cost from above.
Converts rate bounds into total-cost bounds over the specified service life, enabling a guaranteed comparison without exact cost paths.

candidate.question:
Before First Effective Time: “Except as consented to in writing by Parent … the Company shall not:” introduces two prohibitions. Each package triggers both; no other exceptions apply. Controls must address every nitrile–nitride mixing hazard.

Package, controls, written-consent coverage, upfront $k, rate bounds ($k/year)
G, flammable gas, both, 50, [1,2]
U, flammable gas+heat, one, 60, [1,2]
A, flammable gas+heat, both, 100, [2,3]
B, flammable gas+heat, both, 108, [2,4]

Integrable maintenance rates: listed bounds ×(1.10)^t over 0≤t≤5 years, paid continuously. Discount: 10% effective annually; no other costs/residuals.

Which hazards, eligible set, guaranteed cheapest package, and its present-value interval follow?

options.A: Hazards: flammable gas+heat; eligible: {A,B}; cheapest: A; PV: $110–115k.
options.B: Hazards: flammable gas only; eligible: {G,A,B}; cheapest: G; PV: $55–60k.
options.C: Hazards: flammable gas+heat; eligible: {A,B}; cheapest: G; PV: $55–60k.
options.D: Hazards: flammable gas+heat; eligible: {G,A,B}; cheapest: G; PV: $55–60k.

candidate.explanation: Nitrile–nitride mixing presents flammable-gas generation and heat-generation hazards. The project requires controls for both, so G is unsuitable. The written-Parent-consent exception applies to all negative covenants introduced by the preamble. Every package triggers both prohibitions, so U's consent for only one is insufficient. Only A and B are eligible. For an upfront cost I and maintenance rate c(t), present-value cost in $thousands is I + ∫₀⁵ c(t)/(1.10)^t dt. Discounting cancels the growth factor in the rate bounds. Integrating the resulting constant lower and upper bounds over five years gives maintenance intervals G: [5,10], U: [5,10], A: [10,15], and B: [10,20]. Total present-value intervals are therefore G: [55,60], U: [65,70], A: [110,115], and B: [118,128]. Since A's maximum possible cost, 115, is less than B's minimum, 118, A is guaranteed cheapest among eligible packages, regardless of the integrable maintenance paths.

distractor_analysis.reason: Omitting heat generation from the mixing hazards makes G appear adequately controlled -> G is wrongly admitted alongside A and B and has the lowest discounted interval -> the outcome reports flammable gas only, eligibility {G,A,B}, and G at $55–60k.

Correctly identifying both hazards and eligibility {A,B}, but ranking all packages without using that eligibility result -> G's globally lowest interval is selected despite its exclusion -> the outcome reports eligibility {A,B} yet chooses G at $55–60k.

Treating full contractual consent as overriding the separate requirement for heat controls -> G is admitted despite recognition of both hazards and becomes the cheapest admitted package -> the outcome reports both hazards, eligibility {G,A,B}, and G at $55–60k.

True Religion Apparel, Inc. Corporate Responsibility



True Religion Apparel, Inc., together with its subsidiaries and affiliates (collectively, the “Company”), is dedicated to upholding fair and legal employment practices and environmental sustainability requirements.

As an integral component of this commitment, we have developed and implemented an Associate Code of Conduct (the “Code,” available here), which applies to all vendors, manufacturers, contractors, and suppliers (“Associates”) that form a part of our supply chain.

The Code advises our Associates of their obligation to adhere to all applicable local, state (including the California Transparency in Supply Chain Act) and federal laws as well as the standards established by the Company and set forth in the Code.

The core elements of our Code are prohibitions on discrimination, forced labor, and child labor, insistence on fair wages and hours and the provision of safe and healthy working conditions, as well as guidelines for minimizing each Associate’s environmental footprint.

As a condition of doing business with the Company, each Associate must execute the Code and implement the principles contained therein.

The Company will continue to develop Associate monitoring systems including, but not limited to, independent, unannounced third party audits to assess and ensure compliance with the Code.

If the Company determines that any Associate has violated the Code, the Company may either terminate its business relationship or require the Associate to implement a corrective action plan.

By espousing the foregoing principles, the Company strives to ensure integrity of its supply chain while continuing to uphold and exceed the quality of our branded merchandise.



2012 California Transparency in Supply Chain Act (SB 657) (the “Act”)

The Act, which became effective January 1, 2012, requires certain retail sellers and manufacturers to disclose their efforts to eradicate slavery and human trafficking from their direct supply chains. It is intended to provide consumers with the means to determine which companies have an active social responsibility program and thereafter to make conscientious purchasing decisions.

The points outlined below highlight the Act’s mandatory disclosures, followed by an explanation of how the Company is addressing each of them:

(1) Verification

The Company continues to develop monitoring systems to assess and ensure Associate’s compliance with the slavery and human trafficking prohibitions set forth in the Code through various means, including, but not limited to, independent, unannounced on-site third party verification visits.

(2) Audits

The Company relies on independent third party vendors to conducts unannounced audits of Associates, which assist in the evaluation of Associates’ compliance with Company’s supply chain standards for trafficking and slavery.

(3) Integrity of Components

By executing the Code, every Associate certifies that materials incorporated into goods and merchandise manufactured for the Company comply with labor and trafficking laws, and with all other applicable laws, rules and regulations of the respective country or countries in which they do business.

(4) Accountability

Associates must manifest their commitment to the implementation of the Code’s stated anti-slavery and human trafficking principles by maintaining or establishing an appropriate management system (with adequate documentation and record-keeping in place) to address compliance with these principles and detection and correction of any non-compliance.

(5) Training

In connection with its commitment to enforce and uphold the principles set forth in the Code, the Company provides training on recognizing the warning signs of human trafficking and slavery to those employees who have direct responsibility for supply chain management.

CORPORATE RESPONSIBILITY

True Religion Apparel, Inc. Corporate Responsibility



True Religion Apparel, Inc., together with its subsidiaries and affiliates (collectively, the “Company”), is dedicated to upholding fair and legal employment practices and environmental sustainability requirements.

As an integral component of this commitment, we have developed and implemented an Associate Code of Conduct (the “Code,” available here), which applies to all vendors, manufacturers, contractors, and suppliers (“Associates”) that form a part of our supply chain.

The Code advises our Associates of their obligation to adhere to all applicable local, state (including the California Transparency in Supply Chain Act) and federal laws as well as the standards established by the Company and set forth in the Code.

The core elements of our Code are prohibitions on discrimination, forced labor, and child labor, insistence on fair wages and hours and the provision of safe and healthy working conditions, as well as guidelines for minimizing each Associate’s environmental footprint.

As a condition of doing business with the Company, each Associate must execute the Code and implement the principles contained therein.

The Company will continue to develop Associate monitoring systems including, but not limited to, independent, unannounced third party audits to assess and ensure compliance with the Code.

If the Company determines that any Associate has violated the Code, the Company may either terminate its business relationship or require the Associate to implement a corrective action plan.

By espousing the foregoing principles, the Company strives to ensure integrity of its supply chain while continuing to uphold and exceed the quality of our branded merchandise.



2012 California Transparency in Supply Chain Act (SB 657) (the “Act”)

The Act, which became effective January 1, 2012, requires certain retail sellers and manufacturers to disclose their efforts to eradicate slavery and human trafficking from their direct supply chains. It is intended to provide consumers with the means to determine which companies have an active social responsibility program and thereafter to make conscientious purchasing decisions.

The points outlined below highlight the Act’s mandatory disclosures, followed by an explanation of how the Company is addressing each of them:

(1) Verification

The Company continues to develop monitoring systems to assess and ensure Associate’s compliance with the slavery and human trafficking prohibitions set forth in the Code through various means, including, but not limited to, independent, unannounced on-site third party verification visits.

(2) Audits

The Company relies on independent third party vendors to conducts unannounced audits of Associates, which assist in the evaluation of Associates’ compliance with Company’s supply chain standards for trafficking and slavery.

(3) Integrity of Components

By executing the Code, every Associate certifies that materials incorporated into goods and merchandise manufactured for the Company comply with labor and trafficking laws, and with all other applicable laws, rules and regulations of the respective country or countries in which they do business.

(4) Accountability

Associates must manifest their commitment to the implementation of the Code’s stated anti-slavery and human trafficking principles by maintaining or establishing an appropriate management system (with adequate documentation and record-keeping in place) to address compliance with these principles and detection and correction of any non-compliance.

(5) Training

In connection with its commitment to enforce and uphold the principles set forth in the Code, the Company provides training on recognizing the warning signs of human trafficking and slavery to those employees who have direct responsibility for supply chain management.

2012 California Transparency in Supply Chain Act (SB 657) (the “Act”)

The Act, which became effective January 1, 2012, requires certain retail sellers and manufacturers to disclose their efforts to eradicate slavery and human trafficking from their direct supply chains. It is intended to provide consumers with the means to determine which companies have an active social responsibility program and thereafter to make conscientious purchasing decisions.

The points outlined below highlight the Act’s mandatory disclosures, followed by an explanation of how the Company is addressing each of them:

(1) Verification

The Company continues to develop monitoring systems to assess and ensure Associate’s compliance with the slavery and human trafficking prohibitions set forth in the Code through various means, including, but not limited to, independent, unannounced on-site third party verification visits.

(2) Audits

The Company relies on independent third party vendors to conducts unannounced audits of Associates, which assist in the evaluation of Associates’ compliance with Company’s supply chain standards for trafficking and slavery.

(3) Integrity of Components

By executing the Code, every Associate certifies that materials incorporated into goods and merchandise manufactured for the Company comply with labor and trafficking laws, and with all other applicable laws, rules and regulations of the respective country or countries in which they do business.

(4) Accountability

Associates must manifest their commitment to the implementation of the Code’s stated anti-slavery and human trafficking principles by maintaining or establishing an appropriate management system (with adequate documentation and record-keeping in place) to address compliance with these principles and detection and correction of any non-compliance.

In connection with its commitment to enforce and uphold the principles set forth in the Code, the Company provides training on recognizing the warning signs of human trafficking and slavery to those employees who have direct responsibility for supply chain management.

Laboratory (T, rate) records have distinct positive kelvin temperatures and positive rates in fixed units. A proposed workflow sorts whole records by increasing T and plots x = 1/T, y = ln(rate), with two distinct slopes.

1. Classify the sediment as alluvium.
2. Classify mineral loss as diagenetic dissolution.
3. Use simple selection sort for either sequential or linked storage.
4. Use perpendicular Cartesian axes sharing an origin.
5. Traverse sorted records unchanged for left-to-right plotting.
6. Interpret the slope break as possibly indicating a chemical–diffusional regime shift, without establishing its direction.

How many numbered workflow statements are correct?
candidate.explanation: Statements 1, 2, 3, 4, and 6 are correct. Mechanical river deposition produces alluvium, and dissolution is a diagenetic process. Simple selection sort works with sequential and linked storage; sorting whole records retains temperature–rate associations. Cartesian axes are perpendicular and share an origin. Statement 5 is incorrect: for positive T, increasing temperature decreases 1/T, so left-to-right traversal requires reversing the increasing-temperature order. Two Arrhenius slopes can indicate a transition between chemical and diffusional regimes, but do not alone establish its direction. Thus five statements are correct.

distractor_analysis.reason: Incorrectly restricting simple selection sort to sequential storage -> rejects statement 3 in addition to correctly rejecting statement 5 -> counts four correct statements and selects 4.

Recognizing the individual plotting definitions without applying reciprocal monotonicity to record traversal -> incorrectly accepts increasing-temperature traversal as increasing-x traversal in statement 5 -> counts all six statements as correct and selects 6.

Treating the laboratory's chemical rate measurement as the sediment's formation mechanism rather than distinguishing deposition from later alteration -> incorrectly rejects both the alluvium classification and the diagenetic interpretation in statements 1 and 2, while correctly rejecting statement 5 -> counts three correct statements and selects 3.

Edges: X–P, P–Q, X–R, R–S, S–T; U is isolated.

SMILES:
1: CCn1c(SCC(=O)Nc2ccc3c(c2)OCCO3)nnc1-c1ccco1
2: CN(CCc1cn(-c2ccc(F)cc2)c2ccc(Cl)cc12)CCN1CCNC1=O
3: O=C(NC1=NC2CCCCC2N1)c1ccccc1
4: O=S1(=O)C=C(Oc2ccc(F)cc2)c2ccccc21

All annual orders (supplier IDs denote locations):
Supplier, SMILES ID, pounds
P, 1, 2000
Q, 1, 3000
R, 2, 1000
S, 3, 1000
T, 4, 1000
U, 1, 2000

Shipping costs are one annual fixed charge of 16000 yuan plus 0.5 yuan per approved pound, with no other charges. What are the annual budget and average cost per approved pound?
candidate.explanation: SMILES 1 matches the named compound: it contains the benzodioxinyl-substituted acetamide linked through sulfur to the ethyl-furanyl 1,2,4-triazole. The other structures do not have this connectivity. The buyer's connected component is {X, P, Q, R, S, T}; Q is reachable through P, while U is isolated. Thus only the orders from P and Q qualify, totaling 2000 + 3000 = 5000 pounds. Multiplying the weight by 0.5 yuan/pound gives 2500 yuan in variable costs. Adding the single annual fixed charge gives 16000 + 2500 = 18500 yuan. The average rate is total expenditure divided by approved weight: 18500/5000 = 3.70 yuan/pound.

distractor_analysis.reason: Treating reachability as direct adjacency excludes Q despite the path X–P–Q -> only P's 2000 pounds are counted -> 16000 + 0.5 × 2000 = 17000 yuan, and 17000/2000 = 8.50 yuan/pound.

Identifying the matching structure and buyer's connected component but not applying those results to the budget uses all 10000 pounds in the table -> 16000 + 0.5 × 10000 = 21000 yuan, and 21000/10000 = 2.10 yuan/pound.
Mapping the fixed annual charge to each of the two approved supplier vertices instead of charging it once -> 2 × 16000 + 0.5 × 5000 = 34500 yuan -> dividing by 5000 gives 6.90 yuan/pound.

The Company will continue to develop Associate monitoring systems including, but not limited to, independent, unannounced third party audits to assess and ensure compliance with the Code.

If the Company determines that any Associate has violated the Code, the Company may either terminate its business relationship or require the Associate to implement a corrective action plan.

2012 California Transparency in Supply Chain Act (SB 657) (the “Act”)

The Act, which became effective January 1, 2012, requires certain retail sellers and manufacturers to disclose their efforts to eradicate slavery and human trafficking from their direct supply chains. The Company continues to develop monitoring systems to assess and ensure Associate’s compliance with the slavery and human trafficking prohibitions set forth in the Code through various means, including, but not limited to, independent, unannounced on-site third party verification visits.

The Company relies on independent third party vendors to conducts unannounced audits of Associates, which assist in the evaluation of Associates’ compliance with Company’s supply chain standards for trafficking and slavery.

(3) Integrity of Components

Associates must manifest their commitment to the implementation of the Code’s stated anti-slavery and human trafficking principles by maintaining or establishing an appropriate management system (with adequate documentation and record-keeping in place) to address compliance with these principles and detection and correction of any non-compliance.

(5) Training

In connection with its commitment to enforce and uphold the principles set forth in the Code, the Company provides training on recognizing the warning signs of human trafficking and slavery to those employees who have direct responsibility for supply chain management.

options.B: Explosion, fire, heat generation; replace with X.
options.D: Explosion, fire, heat generation; retain under U.
options.C: Explosion, fire, heat generation; retain under R.

The company's budget data for the next year are as follows: number of items shipped 5000, number of sales orders 600, number of shipments 600, total sales amount 1000000 yuan, total shipping volume (pounds) 5000. B.16000
C.4800

screening.question_plan: Ask for a workflow that ranks mutually exclusive annual catalyst-shipping plans by shipping cost per square meter of catalyst metal surface area. First ask which technique is most appropriate among chemisorption, nuclear magnetic resonance, scanning electron microscopy, and X-ray diffraction. Supply each plan's identifier, total shipping weight in pounds, shipment count, and positive total metal surface area reported by chemisorption. Specify an annual fixed shipping cost of 16000 yuan and a variable cost of 0.5 yuan per pound for each alternative. Require calculation of each cost-per-area rate, a direct insertion-sort trace in ascending rate order, and identification of the lowest-rate plan.

answer_plans.plan: Select chemisorption for the metal surface area measurement. For each alternative calculate shipping cost C = 16000 + 0.5W using its annual shipping weight W, then calculate C/A using its total chemisorption-measured metal area A. Report yuan per square meter. Select chemisorption and correctly use area-normalized rates and direct insertion sort, but calculate shipping cost as only 0.5W, omitting the annual fixed cost of 16000 yuan. Consequently rank the plans using incomplete shipping budgets.

Correctly select chemisorption, calculate full shipping budgets and cost-per-area rates, and demonstrate direct insertion sort, but sort the plan records by identifier rather than by the calculated rates. The calculations and algorithm remain disconnected and do not establish the requested cost-effectiveness ranking.

Select chemisorption and calculate full shipping budgets correctly, but divide metal area by shipping cost and sort this reciprocal rate in ascending order. Treat the smallest area-per-yuan value as best, incorrectly relating the mathematical rate and sorting direction to the financial objective.

Express the comparison as yuan per square meter rather than as a dimensionless value.
Evaluate cost divided by metal area to obtain the requested ranking key.

Maintain an ordered prefix of plan records throughout the sorting trace.
Place each next plan record in the sorted prefix according to its cost-per-area key.

financial.necessity: Include the annual 16000-yuan component in each alternative's shipping budget.
Apply 0.5 yuan to each pound shipped, not to each shipment or sales order.
Add fixed and variable shipping costs before normalizing by measured metal surface area.

Calculating the correct rates but sorting records by identifier instead of using those rates disconnects the calculations from the ranking -> insertion prefixes become [P,R] then [P,Q,R] -> the option retains the correct rate vector but incorrectly selects P.

legal.prompt:
CORPORATE RESPONSIBILITY

True Religion Apparel, Inc. Corporate Responsibility



True Religion Apparel, Inc., together with its subsidiaries and affiliates (collectively, the “Company”), is dedicated to upholding fair and legal employment practices and environmental sustainability requirements.

As an integral component of this commitment, we have developed and implemented an Associate Code of Conduct (the “Code,” available here), which applies to all vendors, manufacturers, contractors, and suppliers (“Associates”) that form a part of our supply chain.

The Code advises our Associates of their obligation to adhere to all applicable local, state (including the California Transparency in Supply Chain Act) and federal laws as well as the standards established by the Company and set forth in the Code.

The core elements of our Code are prohibitions on discrimination, forced labor, and child labor, insistence on fair wages and hours and the provision of safe and healthy working conditions, as well as guidelines for minimizing each Associate’s environmental footprint.

As a condition of doing business with the Company, each Associate must execute the Code and implement the principles contained therein.

The Company will continue to develop Associate monitoring systems including, but not limited to, independent, unannounced third party audits to assess and ensure compliance with the Code.

If the Company determines that any Associate has violated the Code, the Company may either terminate its business relationship or require the Associate to implement a corrective action plan.

By espousing the foregoing principles, the Company strives to ensure integrity of its supply chain while continuing to uphold and exceed the quality of our branded merchandise.



2012 California Transparency in Supply Chain Act (SB 657) (the “Act”)

The Act, which became effective January 1, 2012, requires certain retail sellers and manufacturers to disclose their efforts to eradicate slavery and human trafficking from their direct supply chains. It is intended to provide consumers with the means to determine which companies have an active social responsibility program and thereafter to make conscientious purchasing decisions.

The points outlined below highlight the Act’s mandatory disclosures, followed by an explanation of how the Company is addressing each of them:

(1) Verification

The Company continues to develop monitoring systems to assess and ensure Associate’s compliance with the slavery and human trafficking prohibitions set forth in the Code through various means, including, but not limited to, independent, unannounced on-site third party verification visits.

(2) Audits

The Company relies on independent third party vendors to conducts unannounced audits of Associates, which assist in the evaluation of Associates’ compliance with Company’s supply chain standards for trafficking and slavery.

(3) Integrity of Components

By executing the Code, every Associate certifies that materials incorporated into goods and merchandise manufactured for the Company comply with labor and trafficking laws, and with all other applicable laws, rules and regulations of the respective country or countries in which they do business.

(4) Accountability

Associates must manifest their commitment to the implementation of the Code’s stated anti-slavery and human trafficking principles by maintaining or establishing an appropriate management system (with adequate documentation and record-keeping in place) to address compliance with these principles and detection and correction of any non-compliance.

(5) Training

In connection with its commitment to enforce and uphold the principles set forth in the Code, the Company provides training on recognizing the warning signs of human trafficking and slavery to those employees who have direct responsibility for supply chain management.

options.C: Advance candidate A; generic glucose-lowering measurements only; 20,000 yuan, within budget.

Advancing the preferred candidate to this investigation therefore satisfies the budget and sponsor requirement; clinical use is not being recommended.

question:
Accounting measurement is a basic feature of financial accounting, and it occupies an important position in the theory and methods of financial accounting. Which of the following statements about accounting measurement attributes is incorrect? ____
options:
A.Historical cost reflects the past value of an asset.
B.Replacement cost is the current cost of acquiring an identical or similar asset.
C.Present value is the cash or other equivalent that needs to be paid currently to acquire an asset.
D.Fair value refers to the price that would be received to sell an asset or paid to transfer a liability in an orderly transaction between market participants on the measurement date.
answer:
financial.completion:

explanation:
1. Present value refers to the amount obtained by discounting future net cash flows at an appropriate discount rate; it is a measurement attribute that takes into account factors such as the time value of money.

True Religion Apparel, Inc. Corporate Responsibility



True Religion Apparel, Inc., together with its subsidiaries and affiliates (collectively, the “Company”), is dedicated to upholding fair and legal employment practices and environmental sustainability requirements.

As an integral component of this commitment, we have developed and implemented an Associate Code of Conduct (the “Code,” available here), which applies to all vendors, manufacturers, contractors, and suppliers (“Associates”) that form a part of our supply chain.

The Code advises our Associates of their obligation to adhere to all applicable local, state (including the California Transparency in Supply Chain Act) and federal laws as well as the standards established by the Company and set forth in the Code.

The core elements of our Code are prohibitions on discrimination, forced labor, and child labor, insistence on fair wages and hours and the provision of safe and healthy working conditions, as well as guidelines for minimizing each Associate’s environmental footprint.

As a condition of doing business with the Company, each Associate must execute the Code and implement the principles contained therein.

The Company will continue to develop Associate monitoring systems including, but not limited to, independent, unannounced third party audits to assess and ensure compliance with the Code.

If the Company determines that any Associate has violated the Code, the Company may either terminate its business relationship or require the Associate to implement a corrective action plan.

By espousing the foregoing principles, the Company strives to ensure integrity of its supply chain while continuing to uphold and exceed the quality of our branded merchandise.



2012 California Transparency in Supply Chain Act (SB 657) (the “Act”)

The Act, which became effective January 1, 2012, requires certain retail sellers and manufacturers to disclose their efforts to eradicate slavery and human trafficking from their direct supply chains. It is intended to provide consumers with the means to determine which companies have an active social responsibility program and thereafter to make conscientious purchasing decisions.

The points outlined below highlight the Act’s mandatory disclosures, followed by an explanation of how the Company is addressing each of them:

(1) Verification

The Company continues to develop monitoring systems to assess and ensure Associate’s compliance with the slavery and human trafficking prohibitions set forth in the Code through various means, including, but not limited to, independent, unannounced on-site third party verification visits.

(2) Audits

The Company relies on independent third party vendors to conducts unannounced audits of Associates, which assist in the evaluation of Associates’ compliance with Company’s supply chain standards for trafficking and slavery.

(3) Integrity of Components

By executing the Code, every Associate certifies that materials incorporated into goods and merchandise manufactured for the Company comply with labor and trafficking laws, and with all other applicable laws, rules and regulations of the respective country or countries in which they do business.

(4) Accountability

Associates must manifest their commitment to the implementation of the Code’s stated anti-slavery and human trafficking principles by maintaining or establishing an appropriate management system (with adequate documentation and record-keeping in place) to address compliance with these principles and detection and correction of any non-compliance.

(5) Training

In connection with its commitment to enforce and uphold the principles set forth in the Code, the Company provides training on recognizing the warning signs of human trafficking and slavery to those employees who have direct responsibility for supply chain management.

Question: Does the above disclosure meet the following criteria: Does the above statement disclose whether the retail seller or manufacturer requires direct suppliers to certify that they comply with labor and anti-trafficking laws? Reply with either: Yes, No
Answer:

A liquid-fuel store needs four extinguishers operationally, not as a legal minimum. Each weighs 15 lb. Order from one supplier in one shipment; no other costs apply. Its adopted Code requires supplier execution and implementation; execution certifies materials’ compliance with labor and anti-trafficking laws. Alder, Cedar and Dogwood execute and implement it; Birch refuses execution.

Offers (supplier: rating; $/unit; fixed shipping $/shipment; shipping $/lb):
Alder: Class A-only; 50; 10; 0.25
Birch: Class B; 70; 10; 0.25
Cedar: Class B; 80; 40; 0.50
Dogwood: Class B; 90; 10; 0.25

Which eligible supplier offers the lowest delivered cost, and what is that budget?

The fixed shipping charge applies once per shipment. Dogwood therefore offers the lowest eligible delivered cost.

distractor_analysis.reason: Ignore the adopted Code's execution and certification condition while correctly requiring Class B equipment -> treat Birch as eligible and calculate 4 × $70 + $10 + 60 × $0.25 = $305 -> select Birch; $305.

Identify Cedar and Dogwood as eligible and calculate their shipping costs, but rank them using only equipment subtotals of $320 and $360 -> choose Cedar despite its higher delivered total of $390 -> select Cedar; $390.

Apply the four-unit multiplier to the fixed shipment charge as well as the unit price -> calculate Cedar as 4 × ($80 + $40) + 60 × $0.50 = $510 and Dogwood as 4 × ($90 + $10) + 60 × $0.25 = $415 -> select Dogwood; $415.

The Company relies on independent third party vendors to conducts unannounced audits of Associates, which assist in the evaluation of Associates’ compliance with Company’s supply chain standards for trafficking and slavery.

(3) Integrity of Components

By executing the Code, every Associate certifies that materials incorporated into goods and merchandise manufactured for the Company comply with labor and trafficking laws, and with all other applicable laws, rules and regulations of the respective country or countries in which they do business.

(4) Accountability

Associates must manifest their commitment to the implementation of the Code’s stated anti-slavery and human trafficking principles by maintaining or establishing an appropriate management system (with adequate documentation and record-keeping in place) to address compliance with these principles and detection and correction of any non-compliance.

(5) Training

In connection with its commitment to enforce and uphold the principles set forth in the Code, the Company provides training on recognizing the warning signs of human trafficking and slavery to those employees who have direct responsibility for supply chain management.

The Company relies on independent third party vendors to conducts unannounced audits of Associates, which assist in the evaluation of Associates’ compliance with Company’s supply chain standards for trafficking and slavery.

In connection with its commitment to enforce and uphold the principles set forth in the Code, the Company provides training on recognizing the warning signs of human trafficking and slavery to those employees who have direct responsibility for supply chain management.

Working model Decollement/detachment layer refers to a relatively weak rock-structure combination layer above the underlying rock combination, controlled by the overlying folded rock combination, and characterized by strong shear deformation. Multiple detachment layers may develop simultaneously or continuously during lithosphere deformation, and detachment layers may develop on different structural scales, so multi-layer detachment tectonics is the main mode of lithosphere deformation. The discovery of large-scale low-angle faults, such as extensional detachment faults[1,2] and large-scale low-angle thrust faults[3,4], has led structural geologists to propose that the continental lithosphere may be stratified according to physical properties . Therefore, when the lithosphere undergoes large-scale structural deformation, structural detachment may occur along the physical property mutation interface, forming a lithosphere-scale decollement fault. These detachment faults divide the lithosphere into structural layers with different petrophysical properties. Due to the different depths and temperature-pressure conditions of each structural layer, the deformation behavior of each structural layer is also different. A variety of hypothetical models have been proposed for the multi-layer detachment structure of the lithosphere. For example, in the Himalayas, southern Tibet, and other orogenic belts, under the thickening of the lithosphere, it is proposed that the middle-crust channel (or channel) flow model (mid-crustal ductile channel flow) to adjust the excess mass, which explains the phenomenon of the coexistence of surface extension and compression structures[5~7]. Jackson [8]'s continental lithosphere sandwich structure model (Fig. 1) uses the relationship between lithospheric rock physical conditions and temperature and pressure conditions to explain the reasons for the occurrence and existence of delamination structures. Evidence problem
Fig. 1 	Jackson lithosphere sandwich structure model [8] The lithosphere multi-layer detachment structure model has been supported by some field observations and experimental evidence, mainly including: ① Field observation support. Since the deformation traces of the deep structural layers of the lithosphere can be exposed under tectonic action, in some special structural parts, the structural traces formed by different structural layers of the lithosphere during the same tectonic process can "co-exist". A detailed structural analysis of such structural sites, supplemented by analysis of petrology, geochemistry and chronology, can gain new understanding. For example, based on the observation of low-angle normal faults in the North American Cordillera, Wernicke[1] and Lister et al.[2] proposed that low-angle normal faults are ductile shear zones in the middle crust, formed by extensional detachment (Fig. 2), the footwall formed a metamorphic core complex and the hanging wall formed a basin and range structure due to tilting. On the profile, the metamorphic core complex is composed of deep core metamorphic complex, middle-level ductile shear-detachment fault and shallow-level brittle deformation structure, and has the characteristics of three-layer structure. For an in-depth analysis of ductile detachment faults, the type of shear action and its variation can be quantitatively determined by kinematic vorticity, so as to establish a structural kinematic model[7, 9]. In the Hunan-Hubei-Chongqing-Sichuan border area of the middle and upper Yangtze in South China, Yan et al. [10], through the observation and analysis of the relationship between different styles of fault-fold combinations under the condition of thrust and nappe, proposed that the shallow lithosphere structure consists of multiple The thick-skinned-thin-skinned structural model of layered progressive pushover controlled by layer detachment structure (Fig. 3). The above shows that multi-layer detachment tectonics can develop in different structural layers of lithosphere. Fig. 2. 	Three delaminated tectonic models in the formation of low-angle normal faults and metamorphic core complex structures[1,2] Brittle upper crust; 2. Ductile crust; 3. Lithospheric upper mantle; 4. Asthenosphere; 5. Magmatic rock② Evidence from deep geophysical exploration. The most important evidence support for the multi-layer detachment structure of the lithosphere comes from the results of deep geophysical exploration, including deep seismic reflection, magnetotelluric sounding, and Bouguer gravity anomaly detection. After the 5.12 Longmenshan Wenchuan Earthquake in 2008, Burchfiel et al. [11], based on data such as the Bouguer gravity anomaly, believed that the upper crust of Longmenshan did not thicken significantly, but the middle and lower crust with one to several layers of ductile flow crust was flowing eastward. In the process, it was blocked and thickened by the hard central Sichuan block under the Sichuan Basin, resulting in the vertical uplift of Longmenshan and the accumulation of abnormal stress, which eventually led to the Wenchuan earthquake in May 2008. This indicates that there is a multi-layer detachment structure of the lithosphere in the Longmen Mountains and the area to the west. This structural model of Burchfiel et al. [11] further proves that the passage (or channel) flow mode [5~7]. In many mountain ranges, detachment faults have been recognized as one of the dominant factors of orogeny, such as the use of deep reflection seismic profiling (CORCOP) to discover a huge near-horizontal fault beneath the Blue Ridge of the Appalachians in the United States Thrust detachment zone, and pushed the Precambrian crystalline rock series of the Blue Ridge on the sedimentary cover of the Lower Paleozoic, and the thrust distance from the southeast to the northwest of the 5-15km thick foreign rock sheet Up to 260km[3, 4]. ③ Supported by experimental simulation results. In order to verify the multi-layer detachment structure model of the lithosphere, people use petrological and geochemical analysis methods, or carry out relevant high-temperature, high-pressure and petrological experimental analysis on rock samples at different structural levels, and on this basis put forward The delamination structural model of the lithosphere [12] better explains the deep structural detachment of the lithosphere. Figure 3 	Formation model of multi-layered detached nappe thin-skinned structures in the South China Yangtze block [6] Fz, Fc, Fs and Ft represent the structural detachment of the Sinian base, Cambrian base, Silurian and Triassic lower parts, respectively Some key scientific issues involved in the detachment surface[10] Although the multi-layer detachment structural model of the continental lithosphere has been supported by some observations and experimental evidence, there are still some key scientific issues that have not been resolved. Therefore, the multi-layer detachment structural model It is still a working hypothesis. These scientific issues mainly include: ① How to determine the interface properties of structural layer detachment? That is, what is the underground originality? For example, the physical properties and deformation behavior of the structural layer interface are the most critical issues in the deformation of multi-layer detachment structures. What we have observed in the field is the structural traces of the lithosphere exposed to the surface after multi-layer detachment and deformation. However, the interface inferred from deep geophysical data has multiple solutions. How to compare it with surface observations becomes a solution. the crux of the matter. Some researchers have also proposed to use high temperature and high pressure experiments to test. However, due to the limitation of the strain rate and boundary conditions such as temperature and pressure during the experiment, the current simulation is far from the actual environment of natural deformation. ② What is the deformation process of structural layer detachment? That is, what kind of deformation and metamorphism process has it experienced? When we observe on the surface, we invert the deformation process according to some structural kinematics pointing signs during the deformation. However, during the observation process, it was also found that many kinematic directions at the same time were inconsistent or even opposite. In addition, the deformation process we are inverting now does not limit the time and deformation rate, and even completely ignores the deformation process. Therefore, this inversion process may be very different from the natural process. ③ Reasons for deformation differences between structural layers? Among the different structural layers observed in the field, there are huge differences in deformation structural styles and combinations, as well as the metamorphic temperature-pressure conditions reflected by them, but the interface between the two layers, that is, the ductile detachment shear zone, may sometimes only be a few centimeters. What is the reason, what is the tectonic process, and the tectonic force can cause such a huge deformation-metamorphism difference between the upper and lower structural layers? ④ How big is the scale of delamination? Since the multi-layer detachment is based on the observation of low-angle faults, the change and extension scale/depth of low-angle faults are the most important basis for determining the scale of delamination. However, there is no research example so far that can accurately determine The occurrence change and scale of low-angle faults to the deep. Another question related to this is whether this kind of delamination structure only occurs in the middle and upper part of the lithosphere, or can it occur in the entire continental lithosphere? For example, is the delamination at the bottom of the lithosphere[12] a type of delamination tectonics? ⑤ Is there really a middle and lower crustal ductile channel flow in the middle and lower crust? Is it one layer or several layers? Is the multilayer detachment tectonics of the lithosphere controlled by the flow of these ductile flow shells? Or to what extent can the ductile flow crust control the deformation of the lithosphere? How to determine the nature of this fluid? There are no definitive answers to questions about the relative viscosities or rheology of fluids. Since the above key problems have not been resolved, traditional structural geology field observations are limited by surface rock outcrops, there are uncertainties and multi-solutions in the interpretation of deep geophysical detection data, and rock geochemical data have limitations in geological relationship analysis. Insufficient, especially the boundary conditions set by experimental structural geology are far from satisfying the physical, chemical and geological reality of the deep deformation of the continental lithosphere. Therefore, only by combining the studies of structural geology, geophysics and rock geochemistry, and realizing the complementary advantages of multiple disciplines, can objectively carry out more in-depth research on the multi-layer delamination structure of the lithosphere. With the continuous refinement of field structural analysis and the discovery of new important evidence and key structural phenomena, coupled with the continuous application of modern testing and simulation techniques in the field of earth sciences, the temperature-pressure conditions at different depths of the lithosphere and their Morphing features will gradually become a reality. On the basis of these studies, the continental lithosphere multi-layer delamination model will be continuously revised and improved.

Let $f(x, y, z)$ be a bounded function on a bounded closed region $\Omega$ in space. Divide $\Omega$ into $n$ small closed regions $\Delta v{1}, \Delta v{2}, \cdots, \Delta v{n}$, where $\Delta v{i}$ represents the $i$-th small region and also its volume. Choose a point $(\xi{i}, \eta{i}, \zeta{i})$ in each $\Delta v{i}$, make the product $f(\xi{i}, \eta{i}, \zeta{i}) \Delta v{i} (i=1,2, \cdots, n)$, and take the sum $\sum{i=1}^{n} f(\xi{i}, \eta{i}, \zeta{i}) \Delta v{i}$. If, as the maximum diameter among the small closed regions $\lambda \rightarrow 0$, this sum's limit always exists and is independent of the division of the closed region $\Omega$ and the choice of points $(\xi{i}, \eta{i}, \zeta{i})$, then this limit is called the triple integral of the function $f(x, y, z)$ over the closed region $\Omega$, denoted by $\iiint_{n} f(x, y, z) \mathrm{d} v$, that is $\iiint_{\Omega} f(x, y, z) \mathrm{d} v=\lim _{\lambda \rightarrow 0} \sum_{i=1}^{n} f(\xi_{i}, \eta_{i}, \zeta_{i}) \Delta v_{i}, where____is called the integrand?

A.$\Omega$
B.$\mathrm{d} v$
C.$f(x, y, z)$
D.$ f(x, y, z) \mathrm{d} v$

original_candidate.question:
In a metamorphic-core complex, score ductile-detachment regions by the volume integral of modeled plastic-strain contributions from screw dislocations moving under stress. W denotes weak, strongly sheared material between brittle cover and metamorphic core; B denotes shallow brittle material. Cells partition each region with constant, exact data. Tuples give (volume m³, dimensionless contribution, angle between nonzero line/Burgers vectors in degrees, moving:1/0).
Zero-based records:
0 B: (3,2,0,1)
1 W: (2,2,0,1), (1,5,0,0)
2 W: (3,2,90,1)
3 W: (3,2,0,1)
LocateElem searches in order, returning one-based positions (0 if absent). What does it return for score >4 m³?
original_candidate.explanation: W identifies the middle-level ductile shear-detachment setting: relatively weak, strongly sheared material between shallow brittle structures and the metamorphic core. B is excluded. Screw dislocations have helical-ramp geometry with the dislocation line parallel to the Burgers vector; thus the 0° cells are screw-type and the 90° cells are not. Dislocation motion under applied stress contributes to plastic deformation. Define the integrand f as the supplied modeled contribution where a screw dislocation moves under stress, and zero elsewhere. For the cellwise-constant data, the volume integral is exactly the sum of f times cell volume. Subdividing these cells preserves the sum, yielding the same partition-refinement limit as the continuum integral. The algorithm scans region indices in order, skips non-target settings, computes this filtered volume integral, and returns i+1 for the first score strictly greater than 4 m³; if none qualifies, it returns 0. At index 1 the score is 2×2=4 m³, because the other cell is stationary. Equality fails the threshold. At index 2 the score is zero because the dislocations are perpendicular rather than parallel to their Burgers vectors. At index 3 the score is 3×2=6 m³. The first qualifying region therefore has zero-based index 3 and returned one-based position 4.

distractor_analysis.reason: Omitting the geological-setting filter admits the shallow brittle record at index 0 -> its moving screw contribution has volume integral 3×2=6 m³ and passes the threshold -> the returned one-based position is 1.

Recognizing screw geometry, motion, integration, and list indexing separately but failing to use the classification and motion status in the integrand includes every supplied contribution -> the first W record scores 2×2+1×5=9 m³ -> the returned one-based position is 2.

Incorrectly mapping screw helical-ramp geometry to a perpendicular line–Burgers-vector relationship selects moving 90° cells -> index 1 scores zero and index 2 scores 3×2=6 m³ -> the returned one-based position is 3.

question:
Multilayer detachment tectonics of continental lithosphere
answer:
geography.completion:
Working model Decollement/detachment layer refers to a relatively weak rock-structure combination layer above the underlying rock combination, controlled by the overlying folded rock combination, and characterized by strong shear deformation. Multiple detachment layers may develop simultaneously or continuously during lithosphere deformation, and detachment layers may develop on different structural scales, so multi-layer detachment tectonics is the main mode of lithosphere deformation. The discovery of large-scale low-angle faults, such as extensional detachment faults[1,2] and large-scale low-angle thrust faults[3,4], has led structural geologists to propose that the continental lithosphere may be stratified according to physical properties . Therefore, when the lithosphere undergoes large-scale structural deformation, structural detachment may occur along the physical property mutation interface, forming a lithosphere-scale decollement fault. These detachment faults divide the lithosphere into structural layers with different petrophysical properties. Due to the different depths and temperature-pressure conditions of each structural layer, the deformation behavior of each structural layer is also different. A variety of hypothetical models have been proposed for the multi-layer detachment structure of the lithosphere. For example, in the Himalayas, southern Tibet, and other orogenic belts, under the thickening of the lithosphere, it is proposed that the middle-crust channel (or channel) flow model (mid-crustal ductile channel flow) to adjust the excess mass, which explains the phenomenon of the coexistence of surface extension and compression structures[5~7]. Jackson [8]'s continental lithosphere sandwich structure model (Fig. 1) uses the relationship between lithospheric rock physical conditions and temperature and pressure conditions to explain the reasons for the occurrence and existence of delamination structures. Evidence problem
Fig. 1 	Jackson lithosphere sandwich structure model [8] The lithosphere multi-layer detachment structure model has been supported by some field observations and experimental evidence, mainly including: ① Field observation support. Since the deformation traces of the deep structural layers of the lithosphere can be exposed under tectonic action, in some special structural parts, the structural traces formed by different structural layers of the lithosphere during the same tectonic process can "co-exist". A detailed structural analysis of such structural sites, supplemented by analysis of petrology, geochemistry and chronology, can gain new understanding. For example, based on the observation of low-angle normal faults in the North American Cordillera, Wernicke[1] and Lister et al.[2] proposed that low-angle normal faults are ductile shear zones in the middle crust, formed by extensional detachment (Fig. 2), the footwall formed a metamorphic core complex and the hanging wall formed a basin and range structure due to tilting. On the profile, the metamorphic core complex is composed of deep core metamorphic complex, middle-level ductile shear-detachment fault and shallow-level brittle deformation structure, and has the characteristics of three-layer structure. For an in-depth analysis of ductile detachment faults, the type of shear action and its variation can be quantitatively determined by kinematic vorticity, so as to establish a structural kinematic model[7, 9]. In the Hunan-Hubei-Chongqing-Sichuan border area of the middle and upper Yangtze in South China, Yan et al. [10], through the observation and analysis of the relationship between different styles of fault-fold combinations under the condition of thrust and nappe, proposed that the shallow lithosphere structure consists of multiple The thick-skinned-thin-skinned structural model of layered progressive pushover controlled by layer detachment structure (Fig. 3). The above shows that multi-layer detachment tectonics can develop in different structural layers of lithosphere. Fig. 2. 	Three delaminated tectonic models in the formation of low-angle normal faults and metamorphic core complex structures[1,2] Brittle upper crust; 2. Ductile crust; 3. Lithospheric upper mantle; 4. Asthenosphere; 5. Magmatic rock② Evidence from deep geophysical exploration. The most important evidence support for the multi-layer detachment structure of the lithosphere comes from the results of deep geophysical exploration, including deep seismic reflection, magnetotelluric sounding, and Bouguer gravity anomaly detection. After the 5.12 Longmenshan Wenchuan Earthquake in 2008, Burchfiel et al. [11], based on data such as the Bouguer gravity anomaly, believed that the upper crust of Longmenshan did not thicken significantly, but the middle and lower crust with one to several layers of ductile flow crust was flowing eastward. In the process, it was blocked and thickened by the hard central Sichuan block under the Sichuan Basin, resulting in the vertical uplift of Longmenshan and the accumulation of abnormal stress, which eventually led to the Wenchuan earthquake in May 2008. This indicates that there is a multi-layer detachment structure of the lithosphere in the Longmen Mountains and the area to the west. This structural model of Burchfiel et al. [11] further proves that the passage (or channel) flow mode [5~7]. In many mountain ranges, detachment faults have been recognized as one of the dominant factors of orogeny, such as the use of deep reflection seismic profiling (CORCOP) to discover a huge near-horizontal fault beneath the Blue Ridge of the Appalachians in the United States Thrust detachment zone, and pushed the Precambrian crystalline rock series of the Blue Ridge on the sedimentary cover of the Lower Paleozoic, and the thrust distance from the southeast to the northwest of the 5-15km thick foreign rock sheet Up to 260km[3, 4]. ③ Supported by experimental simulation results. In order to verify the multi-layer detachment structure model of the lithosphere, people use petrological and geochemical analysis methods, or carry out relevant high-temperature, high-pressure and petrological experimental analysis on rock samples at different structural levels, and on this basis put forward The delamination structural model of the lithosphere [12] better explains the deep structural detachment of the lithosphere. Figure 3 	Formation model of multi-layered detached nappe thin-skinned structures in the South China Yangtze block [6] Fz, Fc, Fs and Ft represent the structural detachment of the Sinian base, Cambrian base, Silurian and Triassic lower parts, respectively Some key scientific issues involved in the detachment surface[10] Although the multi-layer detachment structural model of the continental lithosphere has been supported by some observations and experimental evidence, there are still some key scientific issues that have not been resolved. Therefore, the continental lithosphere multi-layer detachment structural model It is still a working hypothesis. These scientific issues mainly include: ① How to determine the interface properties of structural layer detachment? That is, what is the underground originality? For example, the physical properties and deformation behavior of the structural layer interface are the most critical issues in the deformation of multi-layer detachment structures. What we have observed in the field is the structural traces of the lithosphere exposed to the surface after multi-layer detachment and deformation. However, the interface inferred from deep geophysical data has multiple solutions. How to compare it with surface observations becomes a solution. the crux of the matter. Some researchers have also proposed to use high temperature and high pressure experiments to test. However, due to the limitation of the strain rate and boundary conditions such as temperature and pressure during the experiment, the current simulation is far from the actual environment of natural deformation. ② What is the deformation process of structural layer detachment? That is, what kind of deformation and metamorphism process has it experienced? When we observe on the surface, we invert the deformation process according to some structural kinematics pointing signs during the deformation. However, during the observation process, it was also found that many kinematic directions at the same time were inconsistent or even opposite. In addition, the deformation process we are inverting now does not limit the time and deformation rate, and even completely ignores the deformation process. Therefore, this inversion process may be very different from the natural process. ③ Reasons for deformation differences between structural layers? Among the different structural layers observed in the field, there are huge differences in deformation structural styles and combinations, as well as the metamorphic temperature-pressure conditions reflected by them, but the interface between the two layers, that is, the ductile detachment shear zone, may sometimes only be a few centimeters. What is the reason, what is the tectonic process, and the tectonic force can cause such a huge deformation-metamorphism difference between the upper and lower structural layers? ④ How big is the scale of delamination? Since the multi-layer detachment is based on the observation of low-angle faults, the change and extension scale/depth of low-angle faults are the most important basis for determining the scale of delamination. However, there is no research example so far that can accurately determine The occurrence change and scale of low-angle faults to the deep. Another question related to this is whether this kind of delamination structure only occurs in the middle and upper part of the lithosphere, or can it occur in the entire continental lithosphere? For example, is the delamination at the bottom of the lithosphere[12] a type of delamination tectonics? ⑤ Is there really a middle and lower crustal ductile channel flow in the middle and lower crust? Is it one layer or several layers? Is the multilayer detachment tectonics of the lithosphere controlled by the flow of these ductile flow shells? Or to what extent can the ductile flow crust control the deformation of the lithosphere? How to determine the nature of this fluid? There are no definitive answers to questions about the relative viscosities or rheology of fluids. Since the above key problems have not been resolved, traditional structural geology field observations are limited by surface rock outcrops, there are uncertainties and multi-solutions in the interpretation of deep geophysical detection data, and rock geochemical data have limitations in geological relationship analysis. Insufficient, especially the boundary conditions set by experimental structural geology are far from satisfying the physical, chemical and geological reality of the deep deformation of the continental lithosphere. Therefore, only by combining the studies of structural geology, geophysics and rock geochemistry, and realizing the complementary advantages of multiple disciplines, can objectively carry out more in-depth research on the multi-layer delamination structure of the lithosphere. With the continuous refinement of field structural analysis and the discovery of new important evidence and key structural phenomena, coupled with the continuous application of modern testing and simulation techniques in the field of earth sciences, the temperature-pressure conditions at different depths of the lithosphere and their Morphing features will gradually become a reality. On the basis of these studies, the continental lithosphere multi-layer delamination model will be continuously revised and improved.

Due to the different depths and temperature-pressure conditions of each structural layer, the deformation behavior of each structural layer is also different. A variety of hypothetical models have been proposed for the multi-layer detachment structure of the lithosphere. For example, in the Himalayas, southern Tibet, and other orogenic belts, under the thickening of the lithosphere, it is proposed that the middle-crust channel (or channel) flow model (mid-crustal ductile channel flow) to adjust the excess mass, which explains the phenomenon of the coexistence of surface extension and compression structures[5~7]. Jackson [8]'s continental lithosphere sandwich structure model (Fig. 1) uses the relationship between lithospheric rock physical conditions and temperature and pressure conditions to explain the reasons for the occurrence and existence of delamination structures. A detailed structural analysis of such structural sites, supplemented by analysis of petrology, geochemistry and chronology, can gain new understanding. For example, based on the observation of low-angle normal faults in the North American Cordillera, Wernicke[1] and Lister et al.[2] proposed that low-angle normal faults are ductile shear zones in the middle crust, formed by extensional detachment (Fig. 2), the footwall formed a metamorphic core complex and the hanging wall formed a basin and range structure due to tilting. On the profile, the metamorphic core complex is composed of deep core metamorphic complex, middle-level ductile shear-detachment fault and shallow-level brittle deformation structure, and has the characteristics of three-layer structure. For an in-depth analysis of ductile detachment faults, the type of shear action and its variation can be quantitatively determined by kinematic vorticity, so as to establish a structural kinematic model[7, 9]. In the Hunan-Hubei-Chongqing-Sichuan border area of the middle and upper Yangtze in South China, Yan et al. [10], through the observation and analysis of the relationship between different styles of fault-fold combinations under the condition of thrust and nappe, proposed that the shallow lithosphere structure consists of multiple The thick-skinned-thin-skinned structural model of layered progressive pushover controlled by layer detachment structure (Fig. 3). This indicates that there is a multi-layer detachment structure of the lithosphere in the Longmen Mountains and the area to the west. This structural model of Burchfiel et al. Anti-Corruption: We expect suppliers to operate with integrity. Suppliers must comply with the U.S. Foreign Corrupt Practices Act as well as any other anti-corruption laws in the jurisdictions in which they do business.

Financial Responsibility: Suppliers are expected to develop and apply appropriate internal controls, accountability and governance models that ensure accurate reporting and encourage financial stability.
